content.user_title: Create Accessible UI Components and Feedback Forms
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent UI components and feedback flows without rebuilding common patterns. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to generate accessible React-oriented UI.
actual_capabilities: Routes component requests to guidance for hero, pricing, features, contact, footer, and header sections.
Routes feedback requests to guidance for feedback, bug report, feature request, and satisfaction forms.
Applies an accessibility checklist for labels, keyboard navigation, focus states, contrast, and screen reader messages.
Supports shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS oriented component generation.
Provides Japanese and English trigger coverage for UI component and feedback form requests.
limitations: It is not intended for authentication, general backend work, database operations, or business logic.
Automatic package installation should be reviewed before any Bash command runs.
The documents provide generation guidance, not a complete design system or production QA process.
Feedback storage and API choices still require project-specific security review.

use_cases.title: Build Landing Page Sections
use_cases.description: Create hero, pricing, features, header, footer, and contact sections that follow accessible UI patterns.

use_cases.title: Add Product Feedback Forms
use_cases.description: Generate feedback, bug report, feature request, or satisfaction form flows for an existing app.

use_cases.title: Improve UI Accessibility
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to add labels, focus states, keyboard support, contrast checks, and readable errors.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a responsive hero section for my product page using accessible labels and clear call to action text.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Feedback Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Add an in-app feedback form with rating, category, message, validation states, and accessible error messages.

prompt_templates.title: Match Existing UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current UI patterns, then create a pricing section that matches spacing, colors, Tailwind usage, and accessibility standards.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Full Feedback Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure feedback collection flow, including UI states, confirmation messages, data fields, and review points before backend work.

output_examples.input: Create a SaaS pricing section with three plans.
output_examples.output: A responsive pricing layout with plan names, feature lists, clear actions, accessible headings, and mobile-friendly spacing.

output_examples.input: Add a bug report form to my app.
output_examples.output: A feedback form flow with issue type, description, severity, contact option, validation messages, and success confirmation.

output_examples.input: Make this contact form more accessible.
output_examples.output: A revised form plan with linked labels, visible focus states, keyboard order, contrast checks, and screen reader friendly errors.

best_practices: Confirm the target component type and existing design system before generating UI.
Review every generated form for labels, focus states, keyboard access, and error handling.
Ask before running package installation or commands that modify project dependencies.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for authentication, database design, or unrelated backend logic.
Do not accept generated package commands without checking the exact dependency changes.
Do not rely on color alone to communicate errors, status, or required actions.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates UI components and feedback form flows for React-style projects.

faq.question: Does it support shadcn/ui?
faq.answer: Yes. The component guidance mentions shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS customization.

faq.question: Can it create feedback forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers feedback forms, bug reports, feature requests, and satisfaction surveys.

faq.question: Does it handle backend implementation?
faq.answer: It is not intended for general backend, database, authentication, or business logic work.

faq.question: How does it address accessibility?
faq.answer: It uses a checklist for alt text, labels, keyboard access, focus states, contrast, and screen reader errors.

faq.question: Is command execution required?
faq.answer: No. Bash is allowed by the skill, but package installation should require explicit review and approval.
